title: Formation of the Yellowstone Caldera
summary: About 640,000 years ago the Lava Creek Tuff eruption, of more than 1000 cubic kilometres, led to the collapse that formed the 45 by 85 km Yellowstone caldera in what is now Wyoming. The USGS places it at the culmination of volcanic activity on the Yellowstone Plateau; the Lunar and Planetary Institute also gives 640,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Both pages give 640,000 years ago, counted back from about 2026 CE (year -637,974), rounded; neither gives an uncertainty.

as_recorded.value: Activity subsequently shifted to the present Yellowstone Plateau and culminated 640,000 years ago
The major eruption at Yellowstone, 640,000 years ago

where.modern_name: Yellowstone Caldera, Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, United States
where.historical_name: Yellowstone Plateau, no polities at this date

importance.justification: The most recent caldera-forming eruption at Yellowstone.

reviewer_note: The USGS page gives more than 1000 km3 for the Lava Creek Tuff and a 45 x 85 km caldera; the LPI page gives more than 300 km3 of ash, so LPI is used for the date only. Pin is the Wikidata point (44.4, -110.7); the caldera is about 85 km long, so uncertainty is 30 km.
